summary.summary: North Norfolk ended 2025/26 as a net investor, not a net borrower: £5.000m of external debt against £37.153m of investments, with debt down from £7.000m a year earlier. The whole £5.000m sits in the under-12-month maturity band - it is a Public Works Loan Board loan (the Treasury's lending arm) running to 1 May 2026 struck at 4.59%, while the one-year PWLB certainty rate had risen to 5.04% by 31 March 2026, so replacing it costs more than it did. Investments beat plan: £1.690m of income against a £1.418m budget, with internally managed cash returning 4.69% against the 4.01% average overnight market benchmark (SONIA), and £20.000m in externally managed pooled funds carrying a £0.458m unrealised gain that the government's IFRS 9 accounting override keeps out of the revenue account until 31 March 2029. Capital spending came in at £13.112m against a £38.280m budget, so the £5.613m of new borrowing the strategy assumed did not happen - only £0.587m of spend went unfinanced - and the council stayed inside its £40.000m authorised borrowing limit all year.

signals.headline: £5.000m - 100% of external debt - falls due within 12 months at 31 March 2026 (up from £2.000m of £7.000m a year earlier); it is the PWLB loan running to 1 May 2026 at 4.59%, against a 1-year PWLB certainty rate of 5.04% at 31 March 2026
signals.why: The entire loan book has to be rolled within weeks of this report at a rate roughly 45 basis points above the one it was struck at, though £37.153m of investments cover the £5.000m several times over so the refinancing is a cost question rather than a liquidity one.

signals.headline: Total external debt fell from £7.000m at 31 March 2025 to £5.000m at 31 March 2026, a £2.0m reduction, with total interest payable of £239,130 for the year and no borrowing in advance of need
signals.why: Gross debt is falling while investments rose to £37.153m, so net investments improved from £20.170m to £32.153m - the balance sheet moved further away from, not towards, borrowing stress.

key_figures.name: capital financing requirement
key_figures.value: £17.794m at 31 March 2026 (31.03.25 actual £17.544m; 2025/26 budget £22.573m in the executive summary table). Appendix A - Annual Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025/26.

key_figures.name: total external debt
key_figures.value: £5.000m at 31 March 2026, all long-term PWLB in the debt portfolio table, against £7.000m at 31 March 2025 (short-term £2.000m + long-term £5.000m). Appendix A.

key_figures.name: maturity under 12m
key_figures.value: £5.000m of £5.000m total borrowing maturing 'Under 12 months' at 31 March 2026, versus £2.000m under 12 months and £5.000m in the 12-24 month band at 31 March 2025; 'Borrowing Limit Exceeded? No'. Appendix A debt maturity table.

key_figures.name: pwlb loan terms
key_figures.value: £5m PWLB loan renewed running from 1 May 2025 to 1 May 2026, secured at an interest rate of 4.59%; taken as a one-year loan rather than rolling short-term borrowing, to avoid locking into a long-term high fixed rate. Appendix A.

key_figures.name: internal borrowing
key_figures.value: Under-funding of CFR £12.794m at 31 March 2026 (gross borrowing £5.000m against CFR £17.794m), up from £10.544m at 31 March 2025 - the authority 'maintained an under-borrowed position' using reserves and cash flow as an interim measure. Appendix A.

key_figures.name: authorised limit and boundary
key_figures.value: Authorised limit £40.000m; maximum gross borrowing position during the year £7.000m; operational boundary £30.000m; average gross borrowing position £5.000m - no breach. Appendix A treasury limits indicator table.

key_figures.name: capital expenditure vs budget
key_figures.value: Capital expenditure £13.112m actual against a £38.280m 2025/26 budget (31.03.25 actual £25.702m); unfinanced capital expenditure (borrowing) £0.587m against a £5.613m budget. Appendix A.

key_figures.name: total investments
key_figures.value: £37.153m total investments at 31 March 2026 (£15.397m money market funds managed in house 42%, £20.000m pooled funds managed externally 53%, £1.756m non-treasury housing loans 5%), against £27.170m at 31 March 2025. Appendix A investment portfolio table.

key_figures.name: treasury outturn vs budget
key_figures.value: Total investment income £1.690m compared to a budget of £1.418m; budget assumption was £29.463m of balances earning an average 3.00%. Appendix A investment outturn.

key_figures.name: investment return vs benchmark
key_figures.value: Internally managed funds earned an average rate of return of 4.69% against the comparable performance indicator, average overnight SONIA, of 4.01%. Appendix A. (The same section states an average internally managed balance of '£36,059', which is inconsistent with the £14.328m average money market fund balance in the interest table on Appendix A p.13 - quoted here only as printed.)

key_figures.name: pooled fund holdings
key_figures.value: £20.000m held in pooled funds at 31 March 2026 (53% of the portfolio; strategic bond £5m, equity income £4m, property £5m, multi-asset income £6m) earning £1.035m at 5.18%; overall fair value gain of £0.458m against an initial total value of £20m (£20.458m); IFRS 9 statutory override extended to 31 March 2029 except for new pooled investments from 1 April 2024. Appendix A (holdings p.11 and p.13; fair value and override p.23).

key_figures.name: la borrowing short term
key_figures.value: £2.000m borrowed from Causeway Coast and Glens Borough Council at 6.35% fixed for 14 days during 2025/26, interest payable £4,871; no local authority borrowing outstanding at 31 March 2026 (£2.000m was outstanding at 31 March 2025 at 5.44%). Appendix A borrowing outturn table.

key_figures.name: interest payable
key_figures.value: Total borrowing interest payable in 2025/26 £239,130 - PWLB £5.000m at 5.39% for 28 days (£23,622), PWLB £5.000m at 4.59% for 335 days (£210,637), Causeway Coast and Glens BC £2.000m at 6.35% for 14 days (£4,871). No debt rescheduling and no early repayments during the year. Appendix A.

key_figures.name: housing association lending
key_figures.value: Five outstanding non-treasury loans to housing providers totalling £1.756m at 31 March 2026 (Broadland Housing £1.346m at 3.80%; four Homes for Wells loans at 3.00%-6.08%, including new loan LN0005 of £0.200m at 6.08% issued in 2025/26), earning £0.072m at a blended 4.07%; loans are set at the PWLB rate so the council does not subsidise them. Appendix A.

key_figures.value: The 31.03.25 capital financing requirement was reduced from the £18.379m stated in the 2024/25 outturn report to £17.544m after an additional 2024/25 capital receipt arrived post-report; the 2024/25 MRP charge was changed as a consequence and the comparative tables restated. Appendix A executive summary.

findings.paper_title: Appx D Reserve Statement Monitoring P4 2026-27
findings.headline: Second Home Premium reserve growing to £1.6m over four years, building dedicated affordable housing funding
findings.detail: The council is building the Second Home Premium reserve from £115k to £1.6m by 2030, adding £285k each year earmarked for affordable housing and homelessness prevention. The forecast movement matches budget, indicating the income is tracking as expected. This shows committed, long-term ringfenced funding for a strategic priority.
findings.matters: A lender would view sustained, dedicated revenue raising for affordable housing and homelessness prevention as evidence of financial discipline and commitment to housing outcomes—a positive financial management signal.
findings.figures: Current balance £115,337; annual additions £285,000; forecast 2030 balance £1,600,337

findings.paper_title: Appx D Reserve Statement Monitoring P4 2026-27
findings.headline: LGR reserve spending only 28% of budget, suggesting local government reorganisation timelines or costs have shifted
findings.detail: The council budgeted £750,000 for Local Government Reorganisation implementation costs but is forecasting only £212,229 will be spent in 2026-27—a £538k underspend (71.7% of budget). This material variance could indicate the reorganisation is delayed, costs are lower than expected, or the scope has changed. The reserve will hold £212k into 2027-28.
findings.matters: LGR is a structural governance change with significant financial implications. A large unplanned underspend raises questions about whether the council's strategic plans for LGR remain on track and whether phased costs will crystallise in future years.
findings.quote: Local Government Reorganisation | To provide for costs associated with the implementation of Local Government Reorgansiation. | 0 | 750,000 | 212,229 | 212,229

findings.paper_title: Appx D Reserve Statement Monitoring P4 2026-27
findings.headline: Capital Projects reserve of £391k completely depleted in current year
findings.detail: The Capital Projects reserve starts 2026-27 at £390,867 and is forecast to reach £0, indicating the council is funding capital developments or asset purchases entirely from this reserve in the current year. This represents either completion of a specific capital scheme or front-loading of capital spend.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand whether the council has a sustainable capital programme and multi-year capital plan. Complete depletion of a capital reserve raises questions about funding for future years' capital needs.
findings.figures: Opening balance £390,867; forecast movement £390,867; closing balance £0

findings.paper_title: Appx D Reserve Statement Monitoring P4 2026-27
findings.headline: Housing reserve drawing £109k more than budgeted, with spending accelerating faster than plan
findings.detail: The Housing reserve is forecast to spend £329,120 against £219,959 budgeted, an additional £109k drawdown. Housing delivery or costs are moving faster than the original budget assumption. The reserve reduces from £1.41m to £1.08m, with further planned draw-downs in future years.
findings.matters: Housing is a material demand area for councils. Faster-than-expected reserve use could signal either successful delivery acceleration or underlying service pressures emerging mid-year.

findings.paper_title: Appx D Reserve Statement Monitoring P4 2026-27
findings.headline: Delivery Plan spending at £472k, nine times the £50k budget, driving acceleration in corporate plan delivery
findings.detail: The Delivery Plan reserve is forecast to spend £472,402 against a budget of £50,000, a variance of £422k. This nine-fold overspend against budget indicates either the Council is accelerating planned deliverables from the Corporate Plan or costs have risen significantly. The reserve depletes from £1.06m to £592k.
findings.matters: A lender would want to know whether the council is delivering corporate priorities on schedule and on budget, or whether cost overruns in corporate delivery are consuming reserves.
